verdicts.strongest_argument: Three separate failures, and the tape one is decisive. (1) The price moved on the penalty, and it moved the other way. The RMB 5.2bn penalty and monopoly finding were published 2026-07-25 (a Saturday). The next admissible session, 2026-07-27, closed at 44.77 against 43.64 on 07-24 - up 2.6% on 6,308,400 shares versus a 1,956,520-share 20-day average - and the stock then rose to 45.31 and 46.00 on 07-28 and 07-29, +5.4% in three sessions on two-to-three times normal volume. The market absorbed a multi-billion-renminbi penalty and a monopoly determination by marking the stock UP, which is the standard repricing when a long-running regulatory overhang is finally quantified. A finding signed negative on that same fact has to explain the volume spike and the direction. (2) The overhang was not new in July. The same admissible document publishes, on 2026-05-06, a securities class action 'over allegedly understating the company's antitrust risk in China despite its dominant market position and alleged monopolistic practices' with a class period running from April 30, 2024, and on 2026-02-26 a sell-side-style note saying 'an ongoing investigation carries too many unknowns. AVOID'. Two years of published antitrust risk is structural and known; the July announcement resolved a magnitude rather than revealing a problem. (3) The timing does not reach this print's P&L. The penalty was announced 2026-07-25, after the June 30 quarter end; the same document shows Q1 was reported around 2026-06-24/25 ('$TCOM (-12.6% pre) Trip.com (TCOM) Lags Q1 Earnings Estimates', 2026-06-25) and that the next report after this one is Q3 on 11/23 (message of 2026-08-25T20:00:20Z). So a 09-02 print covers the June quarter, and a July 25 penalty is a subsequent-event disclosure, not a charge booked in the reported numbers. The finding's phrase 'the first print that has to book the charge' is wrong on the calendar. Finally, the implied-move-versus-realised comparison - 3.5%/$1.61 implied against a 7.1% eight-quarter median with calls leading puts 8:3 - is not the hunter's observation: it is published verbatim in the admissible corpus at 2026-08-26T19:48:20Z, in docs/a8872d46...txt line 8, six sessions before the print. I stop at 85 rather than higher because the take-rate guidance question is real and genuinely undrawn anywhere in this 38-item capture, and because a cheap straddle relative to realised is a variance observation that could be correct even with everything above true.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Publishes the nearly RMB 5.2bn penalty, the monopoly finding, and the exact take-rate/compliance-cost implication the finding quotes - on the day it happened, five weeks before the print.

A securities class action alleging understated Chinese antitrust risk and monopolistic practices, class period from April 30 2024 - the antitrust overhang was public and litigated months before the penalty.
Publishes the entire options comparison: 3.5% / $1.61 implied, calls leading puts 8:3, and a 7.1% median move over the past eight quarters.
Analysts cutting price targets with the stock at its lowest since August 2024 - the de-rating was published and attributed.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The sealed TCOM baseline is one of the two known-defective anchors on this day: event_plausibility is `unknown` with cadence_implausible true, an inferred 17-day gap, and an expected_move_pct of 1.89% built from eight 6-K text matches that are mostly monthly operational updates. I therefore do not use 1.89% for anything, and I note the finding does not lean on it either - it correctly uses the corpus's own 7.1% figure, which is the honest choice. What I do use is the admissible tape, which is unaffected by the anchor defect: 07-24 close 43.64 -> 07-27 44.77 (+2.6%, 6.31m shares vs 1.96m average) -> 07-29 46.00, i.e. +5.4% into the penalty news, then a slow drift to 43.84 on 09-01 (clean-view excludes the 09-02 bar; for a bmo print that close is the reaction). One genuine earnings reaction is visible and dated in the corpus - Q1 on 2026-06-25 at -12.55% on 14.4m shares - which supports the 7.1%-type magnitude and undercuts the baseline's 1.89%.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Confirmation that the 09-02 filing covers a quarter ending after 2026-07-25 (so the penalty is booked rather than disclosed as a subsequent event), plus an explanation of why the stock rose 5.4% on three times normal volume when the penalty was announced.

interactions: Every leg of this finding - the penalty relay, the class action, the options comparison, the valuation anchors and the analyst-target cuts - comes from the single StockTwits document docs/a8872d46...txt, so the 'independence' note describes different messages in one file rather than independent sources.
corpus_limits: Per clean-view/TCOM.json only snapshots 20260831T150636Z and 20260901T150629Z are admissible; I excluded 20260902T150722Z and the 2026-09-02 bar entirely, so nothing from the event day entered my reasoning. TCOM's capture has 38 items, no news documents and no company filing body, so I could not read the penalty announcement itself, confirm the fiscal period the 09-02 filing covers, or find any sell-side note or consensus revenue figure - the fiscal-period point above is inferred from two dated corpus messages, not from a company source, and should be treated as such. The baseline's reaction history is disowned by its own cadence check and I did not use its 1.89% expected move. No options chain, so the 3.5% implied figure rests solely on the third-party relay.
